blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Complex visual question answering often requires vision-language models to think with images, i.e., actively acquire local visual evidence by zooming into informative regions of high-resolution images. Our error analysis shows that many failures in this setting originate from incorrect observation actions, where the model fails to localize key regions or obtain crops that contain sufficient evidence for answering. We further observe that bounding-box tokens exhibit substantially higher generation entropy than ordinary language tokens, indicating high uncertainty when the model decides where to look. However, existing reinforcement learning methods based on final-answer rewards provide only trajectory-level feedback, making it difficult to assign precise credit to the observation actions. We propose Observation Policy Optimization (OPO), an RL algorithm for optimizing observation actions in tool-augmented thinking with images. OPO consists of two core modules. First, Uncertainty-Guided Observation Branching (UOB) treats each image zoom-in tool call as an observation event and selectively branches at high-uncertainty, low-redundancy events during rollout, enabling efficient exploration of alternative cropping decisions and their resulting visual evidence. Second, Evidence-Localized Advantage Attribution (ELAA) compares sibling branches using local evidence-sufficiency rewards and assigns credit only to the corresponding observation-action tokens. By decoupling observation-action optimization from trajectory-level outcome supervision, OPO improves visual evidence acquisition and further enhances visual reasoning performance. Experiments show that OPO consistently improves Qwen3-VL models across scales and achieves competitive performance against larger models and tool-augmented baselines. Code is publicly available.
blocks.zh: 复杂的视觉问题回答往往需要视觉语言模型与图像进行思考,即通过将高分辨率图像放大到信息化区域来积极获取局部视觉证据. 我们的错误分析表明,这种情况下的许多失败源于不正确的观测行动,即模型未能将关键区域本地化或获得含有足够证据的作物来回答. 我们进一步注意到,边框式符号显示的生成均质比普通语言符号要高很多,这表明当模型决定看哪里时,高度不确定性。 然而,基于最终答案奖励的现有强化学习方法只提供轨迹层面的反馈,使得观察行动很难得到准确的功劳. 我们提出观测政策优化(OPO),这是在以图像为工具的思维中优化观测行动的RL算法. OPO由两个核心模块组成. 首先,不确定性指导观测分支(UOB)将每个图像缩放工具调用视为观测事件,并在推出时的高度不确定性和低冗余性活动中有选择地将图像调用视为观测事件,从而能够有效探索替代作物决定及其产生的视觉证据。 第二,证据本地化优势分配(LEAA)利用当地证据充足性奖励来比较兄弟会分支,只给相应的观察行动标志发放信用. 通过将观测-动作优化与轨迹级结果监督脱钩,OPO改进了视觉证据获取,进一步提高了视觉推理性能. 实验显示,OPO不断改进跨尺度的Quen3-VL模型,并实现与更大的模型和工具增强基线相比的竞争性性能. 守则公开发布。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Vision-language models (VLMs) have made substantial progress in visual question answering, chart understanding, document parsing, and complex scene reasoning [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 ] . However, many high-resolution visual tasks cannot be solved from a single global image view. The evidence required to answer a question may appear only in small text, subtle objects, spatial relations, or local image regions. In such cases, models must actively acquire local visual evidence by selecting informative regions and zooming in, an ability often referred to as thinking with images [ 6 , 7 , 8 , 9 , 10 ] .
blocks.zh: 视觉语言模型在视觉问答、图表理解、文档解析和复杂场景推理[1、2、3、4、5]方面取得了实质性进展。 然而,许多高分辨率的视觉任务无法从单一的全球图像角度解决. 回答一个问题所需的证据可能只出现在小的文字,微妙的物体,空间关系,或者局部的图像区域. 在这种情况下,模型必须积极获取当地视觉证据,选择提供信息的区域并放大,这种能力通常被称为用图像思考[6、7、8、9、10]。

blocks.en: In this paper, we study tool-augmented thinking with images, where a VLM invokes an image zoom-in tool during multi-turn reasoning. In this setting, the key challenge is not only to reason over visual evidence, but also to acquire the right evidence in the first place. As shown in Figure 1 (a), our error analysis shows that many failures stem from incorrect observation actions: the model either localizes the wrong region or obtains crops that lack sufficient evidence. We further find that bounding-box tokens exhibit substantially higher generation entropy than ordinary language tokens, as shown in Figure 1 (b), suggesting that visual localization is a high-uncertainty local decision.
blocks.zh: 在本文中,我们用图像研究工具增强的思维,其中VLM在多转折推理时引用图像缩放工具. 在这种背景下,关键的挑战不仅在于理性胜过视觉证据,而且也在于首先获得正确的证据. 如图1(a)所示,我们的错误分析表明,许多失败都是由于不正确的观测行动:模型要么将错误区域本地化,要么获得缺乏充分证据的作物。 我们进一步发现,如图1(b)所示,边框符号显示的生成均匀度远远高于普通语言符号,这表明视觉本地化是一种高度不确定的本地决定。

blocks.en: Existing RL-based methods for visual tool use typically optimize tool-augmented reasoning with trajectory-level rewards, such as final-answer correctness, format validity, or tool-use rewards [ 7 , 8 , 9 , 11 ] . While such rewards can encourage models to use visual tools, they provide imprecise credit assignment for observation actions. A crop that contains sufficient evidence may be penalized if later reasoning fails, while an insufficient crop may be reinforced if the model guesses the answer correctly. This credit mismatch makes it difficult for the model to reliably learn where to look.
blocks.zh: 现有的基于RL的视觉工具使用方法一般以轨迹级别的奖励来优化工具增强的推理,如最终答案正确性,格式有效性,或工具使用奖励[7,8,9,11]. 虽然这种奖励可以鼓励模型使用视觉工具,但它们为观察行动提供了不准确的信用分配。 含有充分证据的作物,如果后来推理失败,可能会受到处罚,而如果模型正确猜测答案,则作物不足可能得到加强。 这种信用不匹配使得模型难以可靠地学习到哪里去寻找.

blocks.en: To address this problem, we propose Observation Policy Optimization (OPO), a reinforcement learning algorithm that directly optimizes observation actions in tool-augmented thinking with images. OPO consists of two complementary modules. First, Uncertainty-Guided Observation Branching (UOB) treats each zoom-in tool call as an observation event and selectively branches from high-uncertainty, low-redundancy events, allowing the model to explore alternative crops from a shared reasoning prefix. Second, Evidence-Localized Advantage Attribution (ELAA) compares sibling branches using local evidence-sufficiency rewards and assigns the resulting advantage only to the observation-action tokens that produced the corresponding crop. Together, UOB and ELAA separate observation-action optimization from trajectory-level outcome supervision, enabling more precise learning of where to look.
blocks.zh: 为了解决这个问题,我们提议观测政策优化(OPO),这是一种强化学习算法,它直接优化了工具增强思维中与图像的观测动作. OPO由两个互补模块组成. 首先,不确定-引导观测分支(UOB)将每个缩放工具调用作为观测事件,并有选择地从高不确定性,低冗余事件分出,使模型能够从共享推理前缀中探索替代作物. 第二,证据本地化优势分配(ELA)利用当地证据充足性奖励比较兄弟会分支,并将由此产生的优势只分配给产生相应作物的观察-行动标志。 UOB和ELAA一起将观测-行动优化与轨迹级结果监督分开,从而能够更准确地了解到哪里去寻找。

blocks.en: We evaluate OPO using Qwen3-VL backbones [ 2 ] on V* [ 12 ] , HR-Bench 4K, and HR-Bench 8K [ 13 ] . OPO consistently improves both model scales, increasing overall accuracy by 10.0, 12.4, and 15.8 percentage points for Qwen3-VL-2B and by 4.7, 4.1, and 4.3 percentage points for Qwen3-VL-8B on the three benchmarks, respectively. OPO-8B also achieves competitive performance against strong open-source, proprietary, and tool-augmented baselines across these benchmarks. Ablation studies further show that uncertainty-guided observation branching and evidence-localized advantage attribution both contribute to these gains.
blocks.zh: 我们使用Qune3-VL骨干对OPO进行评估 [2]在V* [12],HR-Bench 4K,HR-Bench 8K [13]. OPO不断改进两个模型表,在三个基准上,Qune3-VL-2B的总精度分别提高10.0、12.4和15.8个百分点,Qune3-VL-8B的精度分别提高4.7、4.1和4.3个百分点。 OPO-8B还对照强有力的开放源码、专有性和工具强化基线,在这些基准上取得了竞争力。 对比研究进一步表明,不确定性导向观测分支和证据本地化优势归属都有助于这些收益。

blocks.en: Our contributions are summarized as follows: • We identify observation actions as a key bottleneck in thinking with images. Our analysis shows that many failures stem from insufficient visual evidence acquisition, and that observation-action tokens exhibit high local uncertainty. • We propose OPO, which consists of two complementary modules: Uncertainty-Guided Observation Branching for targeted exploration of alternative cropping decisions, and Evidence-Localized Advantage Attribution for precise credit assignment. • Experiments show that OPO consistently improves Qwen3-VL models across scales and achieves competitive performance against much larger models and tool-augmented methods.
blocks.zh: • 我们的贡献概述如下: 我们认为,观察行动是用图像思考的一个关键瓶颈。 我们的分析表明,许多失败是由于无法充分获取视觉证据,而观察行动标志显示出高度的局部不确定性。 我们提议由两个补充单元组成业务方案办公室: 不确定 -- -- 指导性意见 分立,有针对性地探索其他作物种植决定,以及确定信贷分配的循证当地优惠分配。 • 实验表明,OPO不断改进跨尺度的Quen3-VL模型,并实现与更大的模型和工具强化方法相比的竞争性能。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Thinking with images extends multimodal reasoning by allowing models to acquire and manipulate visual evidence during inference [ 10 ] . Within this paradigm, visual exploration methods use crops, zooming, and other image operations to inspect details that may be lost in the global view [ 14 , 15 , 16 ] . DeepEyes learns a zoom-based observation policy through reinforcement learning [ 7 ] . Broader tool interfaces support more diverse evidence acquisition: Thyme uses executable code for image manipulation and computation [ 17 ] , while DeepEyesV2 and SenseNova-MARS combine visual operations with search [ 18 , 19 ] . Alongside these interactive approaches, latent visual reasoning explores internal visual representations [ 20 ] , and ZwZ distills region-level supervision into the model to enable single-pass perception without inference-time zooming [ 21 ] .
blocks.zh: 与图像的思考通过允许模型在推论中获取和操纵视觉证据来扩展多式联运推理[10]. 在这个范式中,视觉探索方法利用农作物,放大,以及其他图像操作来检查全球视野中可能丢失的细节[14,15,16]. DeepEyes通过强化学习学习,学习以放大为基础的观测政策[7]. 更广泛的工具接口支持更多样化的证据获取: Thyme使用可执行代码进行图像操纵和计算[17],而DeepEyesV2和SenseNova-MARS则将视觉操作与搜索[18,19]相结合. 除了这些交互方法外,潜伏的视觉推理还探索了内部的视觉表现[20],ZwZ将区域层面的监督分解到模型中,以便能够在不进行推论时间缩放的情况下实现单通过感知[21].

blocks.en: A related question is how to supervise the visual actions taken during reasoning. CodeVision and CodeV address this through process rewards for code-based tool use. CodeVision rewards tool-use strategy and efficiency, including improvements in crop overlap with a target region [ 22 ] . CodeV evaluates the evidence provided by tool outputs and combines these scores with answer correctness to form a trajectory-level advantage [ 23 ] . OPO connects evidence supervision to the observation decision itself: it explores alternative crops from a shared reasoning prefix, compares their evidence sufficiency within the resulting sibling group, and assigns the local advantage to the corresponding observation-action tokens. This couples the exploration of candidate observations with credit assignment for the evidence they acquire.
blocks.zh: 一个相关的问题是,如何监督推理过程中采取的视觉行动。 CodeVision和CodeV通过对基于代码的工具使用的流程奖励来解决这个问题. 守则奖励工具使用战略和效率,包括改进作物与目标区域的重叠[22]。 CodeV评价工具输出提供的证据,将这些分数与答案正确性结合起来,形成轨迹级优势[23]. OPO将证据监督与观察决定本身联系起来:它从共同推理前缀中探索替代作物,比较其由此产生的兄弟姐妹组内的证据充足性,并将本地优势分配给相应的观察-动作符号. 这对候选人意见的探究和获得的证据的信用分配。

blocks.en: Agentic reinforcement learning formulates large language models as learnable policies embedded in multi-turn interactive environments, enabling them to plan, reason, and invoke tools under partial observations [ 24 ] . More broadly, reinforcement learning has also found applications in other domains [ 25 , 26 , 27 ] . Early tool-augmented agents mainly relied on prompting or supervised fine-tuning to elicit tool-use behaviors, such as ReAct, Toolformer, FireAct, AgentTuning, and Agent-FLAN [ 28 , 29 , 30 , 31 , 32 ] . Recent studies further apply reinforcement learning to multi-turn tool interaction, using outcome or rule-based rewards to train models to autonomously invoke search engines, browsers, code interpreters, or visual tools for complex reasoning, information seeking, and multimodal tasks [ 33 , 34 , 35 , 36 , 37 , 38 , 39 , 40 , 7 , 41 ] . ARPO and AEPO further leverage token entropy to improve multi-turn tool-use exploration through branch sampling or entropy-balanced optimization at high-uncertainty tool-call steps [ 42 , 43 ] . While these methods target general tool-use behavior, OPO specializes agentic RL to visual observation: it uses uncertainty-guided branching to explore alternative crops and evidence-localized attribution to assign feedback according to the visual evidence produced by the observation action.
blocks.zh: 代理强化学习将大型语言模型发展成为嵌入多回合互动环境中的可学习政策,使他们能够在部分观察下进行规划,理性,并引用工具[24]. 更广泛地说,强化学习在其他领域也有应用[25、26、27]。 早期工具强化剂主要依靠提示或监督的微调来诱导工具使用行为,如ReAct, Toolformer, FireAct, AgentTuning, Agent-FLAN [28, 29, 30, 31, 32]. 最近的研究进一步将强化学习应用于多回合工具交互,利用成果或基于规则的奖励来训练模型自主地引用搜索引擎,浏览器,代码解释器,或视觉工具来进行复杂的推理,信息搜索,以及多式联运任务[33,34,35,36,37,38,39,40,7,41]. ARPO和AEPO通过分支采样或在高不确定度工具调用步骤下对Entropy进行平衡优化,进一步利用象征性的Entropy来改进多回合工具使用探索[42,43]. 虽然这些方法针对一般的工具使用行为,但OPO专门将代理RL用于视觉观察:它使用不确定性引导分支来探索替代作物和证据本地化的归属,根据观测动作产生的视觉证据来分配反馈.

blocks.en: 3 Preliminary Analysis
blocks.zh: 3 初步分析

blocks.en: 3.1 Observation Events and Observation-Action Tokens
blocks.zh: 3.1 观察事件和观察行动

blocks.en: We follow the image zoom-in tool interface of Qwen3-VL [ 2 ] , where the model generates tool-call tokens in a predefined format to trigger a zoom-in operation. Each tool call contains a region label, a bounding box, and an image index, which together determine the local visual evidence the model will observe next. We refer to each valid image zoom-in tool call as an observation event , and call its region-label, bounding-box and image-index tokens observation-action tokens . The concrete tool-call schema, prompt template, and zoom-in tool behavior are provided in Appendix E .
blocks.zh: 我们跟随Qwen3-VL [2] 的图像缩放工具界面,模型在其中以预定义的格式生成工具调用符,以触发缩放操作. 每个工具调用都包含一个区域标签,一个边框,和一个图像索引,它们共同决定了模型接下来将观察到的局部视觉证据. 我们把每个有效的图像缩放工具呼叫称为观察事件, 具体的工具调用方案、即时模板和缩放工具行为载于附录E。

blocks.en: 3.2 Failure Analysis on V*
blocks.zh: 3.2 对V的失败分析*

blocks.en:
We analyze the error trajectories of Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct [ 2 ] and a Qwen3-VL-8B model trained under the DeepEyes [ 7 ] paradigm on the V* [ 12 ] dataset, aiming to understand the main sources of failure in tool-augmented visual reasoning. We focus on whether the model’s image zoom-in operation acquires local visual evidence sufficient to answer the question. Specifically, we categorize a trajectory as an observation error if the model localizes an irrelevant region that does not contain the key evidence required for answering the question. If the cropped region contains sufficient evidence but the model still fails in subsequent reasoning or answer generation, we categorize it as a reasoning error.
As shown in Figure 1 (a, top), Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct achieves an answer accuracy of 87.96% on V*. Among its incorrect answers, approximately 74% of failures are mainly caused by observation errors. For the Qwen3-VL-8B model trained under the DeepEyes paradigm, the answer accuracy improves to 90.05%, yet approximately 79% of its incorrect answers still mainly originate from observation errors.
These results indicate that although outcome-level RL can improve final-answer accuracy, failures remain concentrated in the local visual evidence acquisition stage. Therefore, the training process needs to provide more direct optimization signals for the observation actions that determine where the model looks. Localization failures also dominate unsuccessful trajectories in stronger models (Appendix I ).
blocks.zh:
我们分析Qwen3-VL-8B-Instructionct [2]的误差轨迹,以及一个在DeepEyes [7]范式下在V* [12]数据集上训练的Quen3-VL-8B模型,目的是了解工具强化视觉推理中失败的主要来源. 我们专注于模型的图像缩放操作是否获得足以回答问题的局部视觉证据. 具体地说,如果模型将一个不相关的区域本地化,而不包含回答问题所需的关键证据,我们就将一个轨迹归类为观测错误. 如果裁剪区域包含足够的证据,但模型在后续推理或答案生成中仍然失败,我们把它归类为推理错误.
如图1(a,上)所示,Quen3-VL-8B-Instruct在V*上的答题精度达到87.96%. 在其不正确的答案中,大约74%的失败主要是观测错误造成的. 对于在DeepEyes范式下培训的Qune3-VL-8B模型,答案精度提高到90.05%,但其不正确的答案中约79%仍然主要源于观测错误.
这些结果表明,虽然成果级RL可以提高最终答案的准确性,但失败仍然集中在当地视觉证据获取阶段. 因此,培训过程需要为决定模型外观位置的观测行动提供更直接的优化信号. 本地化失败也主宰了较强模型中不成功的轨迹(附录一.

blocks.en: As shown in Figure 1 (b, bottom), the bounding-box tokens used for localization in observation actions exhibit substantially higher entropy than ordinary reasoning tokens. We conduct this analysis over all samples in the V* [ 12 ] dataset. The bounding-box tokens have a mean entropy of 0.522 and a median entropy of 0.501, both more than twice the corresponding mean entropy of 0.229 and median entropy of 0.225 for reasoning tokens. The event-aligned trace in Figure 1 (b, top) further shows that entropy spikes concentrate on bounding-box tokens, which directly determine where the model looks. blocks.en: Observation Policy Optimization (OPO) is a reinforcement learning framework that improves where a model looks during tool-augmented thinking with images. Following the definition above, we denote each candidate observation event by e e . OPO introduces two complementary modules for optimizing the model’s observation actions: Uncertainty-Guided Observation Branching (UOB, Section 4.1 ) and Evidence-Localized Advantage Attribution (ELAA, Section 4.2 ). The full training procedure is summarized in Appendix A.1 .

blocks.en: 4.1 Uncertainty-Guided Observation Branching
blocks.zh: 4.1 不明确的观察分支

blocks.en: UOB is a rollout-time module for targeted exploration around uncertain observation events. Instead of spending all M M samples on independent full-trajectory rollouts, UOB first obtains a small set of base trajectories and then uses the remaining budget to branch at high-uncertainty observation events while filtering redundant child candidates. This preserves the same reasoning prefix while varying the observation action, making the resulting sibling trajectories directly comparable. As a result, UOB concentrates exploration on observation decisions where the model is most unsure, avoids spending rollout budget on redundant crops, and produces branch groups that provide controlled comparisons for ELAA.
blocks.zh: UOB是一个推出时间模块,用于围绕不确定的观测事件进行有针对性的探索. UOB没有将所有的MM样本都花在独立的全射线推广上,而是首先获得一小组基础轨迹,然后在高不确定性的观察活动中使用剩余的预算进行分支,同时过滤多余的儿童候选者. 这在改变观测动作的同时保留了相同的推理前缀,使得由此而来的立体轨迹可以直接比较. 因此,UOB集中探索模型最不确定的观测决定,避免将推广预算花在多余作物上,并产生分支组,为ELA提供可控比较.

blocks.en: For each question, OPO produces M M trajectories under a fixed rollout budget. It first samples B B base trajectories and reserves the remaining P = M − B P=M-B rollout slots for observation-event branching and backfill. Each base trajectory is decoded until it reaches the first valid observation event or terminates without invoking the zoom-in tool. For each collected event, we record the shared pre-tool prefix, the generated observation-action spans, and the original candidate crop. These event records provide the basis for UOB to branch from the shared pre-tool prefix and for ELAA to attribute local feedback to the corresponding observation-action tokens.

blocks.en: ELAA converts the sibling trajectories produced by UOB into local advantages for observation-action tokens. Trajectories in the same branch group share the same pre-tool prefix, but may generate different observation actions and crops. ELAA first evaluates each crop with an evidence-sufficiency reward, then normalizes these local scores within the branch group to obtain a group-local advantage. Finally, this local advantage is applied only to the observation-action token spans that produced the corresponding crop, while the remaining generated tokens keep the global outcome advantage.

blocks.en: 5.1 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 5.1 实验设置

blocks.en: To comprehensively assess the effectiveness of OPO, we compare it against three categories of baselines. First, we include advanced proprietary models, including GPT-5 mini and GPT-5.2 [ 44 , 45 ] , Claude Opus 4.6 [ 46 ] , and Gemini-3 Pro [ 47 ] , which represent strong closed-source general-purpose vision-language systems. Second, we compare with state-of-the-art open-source vision-language models, including LLaVA-OneVision [ 48 ] , Qwen2.5-VL [ 1 ] , Qwen3-VL [ 2 ] , Qwen3.5 [ 49 ] , and Kimi K2.5 [ 50 ] . Third, we consider methods explicitly designed with workflows or tool-use procedures, including SEAL [ 12 ] , DyFo [ 51 ] , ZoomEye [ 52 ] , DeepEyes [ 7 ] , and DeepEyesV2 [ 18 ] . These workflow-based systems are particularly relevant because they also aim to improve fine-grained perception by changing how visual evidence is acquired or processed.
blocks.zh: 为了全面评估业务方案办公室的有效性,我们将其与三类基线进行比较。 第一,我们包括先进的专有型号,包括GPT-5微型和GPT-5.2[44,45],克劳德·奥普斯4.6[46],和双子座-3 Pro[47],它们代表着强大的闭源通用视觉语言系统. 第二,我们比较最先进的开源视觉语言模型,包括LLaVA-One Visions [48],Quen2.5-VL [1],Quen3-VL [2],Quen3.5 [49],和Kimi K2.5 [50]. 第三,我们考虑明确采用工作流程或工具使用程序的方法,包括海豹突击队[12]、DyFo[51]、ZomEye[52]、DeepEyes[7]和DeepEyesV2[18]。 这些基于工作流程的系统特别相关,因为它们也旨在通过改变视觉证据的获取或处理方式来改善精细的感知.

blocks.en: Since fine-grained high-resolution perception tasks naturally test a model’s ability to observe visual details, we evaluate models on three popular benchmarks: V* [ 12 ] , HR-Bench 4K, and HR-Bench 8K [ 13 ] . Details of these benchmarks are provided in Appendix B , and the evaluation protocol is described in Appendix C .

blocks.en: For readability, we denote Qwen3-VL-2B/8B trained with OPO as OPO-2B/8B.

blocks.en: Table 1 presents the main results of OPO on high-resolution perception benchmarks. Overall, OPO consistently improves performance across model scales and datasets. Based on Qwen3-VL-2B, OPO-2B improves the overall accuracy on V*, HR-Bench 4K, and HR-Bench 8K by 10.0, 12.4, and 15.8 points, respectively. Based on Qwen3-VL-8B, OPO-8B also brings gains of 4.7, 4.1, and 4.3 points. The gains suggest that observation-action optimization is particularly effective for acquiring fine-grained visual evidence in high-resolution settings. These results show that OPO substantially improves smaller models while remaining effective at larger scales.
blocks.zh: 表1列出业务干事关于高分辨率感知基准的主要结果。 总体而言,业务执行办公室不断改进模型尺度和数据集的绩效。 基于Quen3-VL-2B,OPO-2B在V*,HR-Bench 4K,HR-Bench 8K上的总精度分别提高了10.0,12.4和15.8分. 基于Quen3-VL-8B,OPO-8B也带来了4.7,4.1和4.3分的收获. 成果表明,观测行动优化对于在高分辨率环境中获取精细的视觉证据特别有效。 这些结果显示,业务方案办公室大大改进了较小的模式,同时在更大的规模上仍然有效。

blocks.en: Compared with strong open-source and proprietary models, OPO-8B also achieves competitive performance. On V*, OPO-8B obtains 92.7% overall accuracy, outperforming several strong baselines, including Gemini-3 Pro, Qwen3-VL-32B, and Qwen3.5, while remaining below the much larger Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B and the Code-enabled Qwen3.5. On HR-Bench 4K, OPO-8B reaches 85.5% overall accuracy, achieving the best result in the table and slightly surpassing Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B at 85.4%. On HR-Bench 8K, OPO-8B improves Qwen3-VL-8B from 76.5% to 80.8%, approaching the performance of much larger models. These results suggest that directly optimizing observation actions can effectively improve high-resolution visual evidence acquisition, rather than relying solely on scaling model size.
blocks.zh: 与强大的开源和专有模式相比,OPO-8B也实现了竞争性能. 在V*上,OPO-8B获得92.7%的整体准确度,表现优于几个强基线,包括双子座-3 Pro,Quen3-VL-32B,以及Quen3.5,同时仍然低于更大的Quen3-VL-235B-A22B和密码驱动的Quen3.5. 在HR-Bench 4K上,OPO-8B达到总精度的85.5%,在表中取得了最佳成绩,并以85.4%的精度略高于Qune3-VL-235B-A22B. 在HR-Bench 8K上,OPO-8B改进了Quen3-VL-8B,从76.5%提高到80.8%,接近了更大模型的性能. 这些结果表明,直接优化观测行动可以有效地改进高分辨率的视觉证据获取,而不是完全依靠模型大小的缩放.

blocks.en: OPO-8B also compares favorably with other specialized visual reasoning methods. SEAL, DyFo, ZoomEye, DeepEyes, DeepEyesV2, Thyme-RL, and SenseNova-MARS improve fine-grained visual perception through visual search, dynamic focusing, or tool use, while ZwZ distills region-level supervision into the model for single-pass perception without tools. OPO-8B achieves 92.7% and 85.5% overall accuracy on V* and HR-Bench 4K, respectively, ranking first among these methods on both benchmarks; on HR-Bench 8K, it achieves 80.8%, second only to ZwZ-8B. Notably, OPO-2B achieves 78.4% and 76.4% on HR-Bench 4K and 8K, outperforming several 7B baselines. These results show that targeted observation exploration and localized credit attribution enable OPO to improve the acquisition and use of fine-grained visual evidence.
blocks.zh: OPO-8B也与其他专业的视觉推理方法相比较为有利. 海豹突击队,DyFo,ZoomEye,DeepEyes,DeepEyesV2,Thyme-RL,以及SenseNova-MARS通过视觉搜索,动态聚焦,或工具使用,改进了精致的视觉感知,而ZwZ则将区域层面的监管蒸馏成没有工具的单通过感知模型. OPO-8B在V*和HR-Bench 4K上的总精度分别达到92.7%和85.5%,在这两种基准上在这两种方法中排名第一;在HR-Bench 8K上,它达到80.8%,仅次于ZwZ-8B. 值得注意的是,OPO-2B在HR-Bench 4K和8K上的成绩分别达到78.4%和76.4%,超过了几个7B基线。 这些结果表明,有针对性的观察探索和本地化的信用归属使OPO能够改进精细视觉证据的获取和使用.

blocks.en:
Table 2 further provides a controlled comparison between OPO and DeepEyes-style outcome-level GRPO. The DeepEyes results in Table 1 are taken from the original paper, whereas the DeepEyes-style GRPO baselines in Table 2 are retrained by us under the same backbone, training budget, and zoom-tool setup as OPO. DeepEyes-style GRPO relies only on outcome-level rewards such as final-answer correctness, format quality, and tool-use signals. In contrast, OPO further introduces uncertainty-guided local branching and evidence-localized attribution.
Although DeepEyes-style GRPO performs better on a few subtasks, OPO is more stable in terms of overall accuracy, especially on HR-Bench. This suggests that outcome-level rewards can encourage the model to use the zoom-in tool, but they still struggle to assign local evidence-quality feedback to the specific observation actions. By exploring alternative crops around high-uncertainty observation events and applying evidence-sufficiency feedback to the corresponding observation-action tokens, OPO more effectively optimizes where the model looks.

虽然深眼式 GPRO在一些子任务上表现较好,OPO在总体准确性上更为稳定,特别是在HR-Bench上. 这表明成果级奖励可以鼓励模型使用缩放工具,但它们仍然难以为具体的观察行动分配当地的证据质量反馈. 通过围绕高不确定性观测事件探索替代作物,并将证据充足反馈应用于相应的观测-动作符号,OPO可以更有效地优化模型外观位置.

blocks.en: Since ELAA relies on sibling trajectories produced by UOB for local comparison, we do not remove UOB alone; instead, we jointly remove UOB and ELAA. Without UOB and ELAA, the model degenerates into DeepEyes-style outcome-level GRPO training [ 7 ] . This variant performs substantially worse than the full OPO on all three benchmarks, suggesting that ordinary full-trajectory sampling is insufficient for exploring alternative observation actions, especially in high-resolution tasks where an incorrect crop can directly affect the final answer.
blocks.zh: 由于ELA依赖于UOB制作的姊妹轨迹进行局部比较,所以我们不单独去除UOB;相反,我们联合去除UOB和ELA. 没有UOB和ELA,该模式退化为DeepEyes式的成果级GPRO培训[7]. 这一变式在所有三个基准上都表现大大低于整个OPO,表明普通的全射线取样不足以探索其他观测行动,特别是在高分辨率任务中,如果作物不正确会直接影响最后答案。

blocks.en: Removing ELAA keeps the UOB branching mechanism but removes localized evidence attribution, so the evidence-sufficiency feedback is no longer applied specifically to observation-action tokens and instead becomes a trajectory-level signal. This variant still shows consistent degradation compared with the full method, indicating that outcome-level or trajectory-level supervision alone can cause credit mismatch between observation actions and downstream reasoning. Meanwhile, w/o ELAA remains better than w/o UOB & ELAA, suggesting that UOB’s local branching itself is beneficial, but ELAA is needed to more effectively convert local evidence quality into observation-action learning signals.
blocks.zh: 移除ELA保留UOB分支机制,但去除本地化的证据归属,因此证据充足性反馈不再专门应用于观测-动作符号,转而成为轨迹级信号. 这一变式仍然显示出与全方法相比的不断退化,表明仅结果一级或轨迹一级监督就会导致观测行动和下游推理之间的信用不匹配。 与此同时,W/o ELAA仍然比W/o UOB & LEAA好,这表明UOB的本地分支本身是有好处的,但需要ELAA将本地证据质量更有效地转化为观察-行动学习信号.

blocks.en: We further examine the design choices inside UOB. Replacing uncertainty-guided event selection with random branching reduces performance, indicating that high-entropy observation events are more informative branching points than randomly selected zoom events. Removing redundancy filtering also hurts performance, suggesting that without penalizing crops that heavily overlap with previous observations, the limited branching budget can be wasted on redundant visual regions.
blocks.zh: 我们进一步审查UOB内部的设计选择. 以随机分支取代不确定性引导的事件选择会降低性能,表明高强度观测事件比随机选择的缩放事件更能提供信息的分支点. 取消冗余过滤也伤害了性能,说明如果不惩罚与先前观测高度重叠的作物,有限的分支预算可能会浪费在多余的视觉区域.

blocks.en: We also analyze the effect of rollout budget and base-trajectory allocation. The smaller setting ( M = 4 , B = 1 ) (M=4,B=1) performs worse, showing that insufficient rollout budget limits local observation exploration. When fixing M = 8 M=8 , using only B = 1 B=1 provides too few base candidates and may miss useful observation events, while increasing to B = 4 B=4 reduces the budget available for local branching and limits the exploration of alternative crops. The default setting M = 8 , B = 2 M=8,B=2 achieves a better balance between base-candidate coverage and event-local branching. Increasing the budget to M = 16 , B = 2 M=16,B=2 brings only marginal gains, suggesting diminishing returns from larger rollout budgets.
blocks.zh: 我们还分析推出预算和基础-外延分配的影响。 较小的设置(M=4,B=1)(M=4,B=1)表现更糟糕,表明推出预算不足限制了局部观测探索. 在修复M=8 M=8时,只使用B=1 B=1提供太少的基选,可能错过有用的观测事件,而增加至B=4 B=4则会减少可用于当地分枝的预算,限制对替代作物的探索. 默认设置 M = 8, B = 2 M = 8, B = 2 实现了基础-candidate覆盖与事件-局部分支的较好平衡. 将预算增加至M=16,B=2M=16,B=2只带来微小收益,表明较大推出预算的回报减少.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
In this work, we study a key challenge in tool-augmented thinking with images: models must learn not only how to reason, but also where to look during reasoning. We show that many failures in high-resolution fine-grained visual tasks originate from the observation stage rather than downstream language reasoning, and that the observation-action tokens determining local crops exhibit substantially higher uncertainty than ordinary language tokens. These findings suggest that visual evidence acquisition is a critical decision-making process that should be optimized directly, rather than treated as an ordinary part of trajectory-level generation.
Based on these observations, we propose Observation Policy Optimization (OPO), which improves visual evidence acquisition through uncertainty-guided observation branching and evidence-localized advantage attribution. OPO performs local branching at high-uncertainty and low-redundancy observation events, allowing the model to explore alternative crops from shared reasoning prefixes. It then assigns evidence-sufficiency feedback only to the observation-action tokens that produce the corresponding crops, thereby reducing the credit mismatch between final-answer rewards and local evidence quality.
Experiments across high-resolution visual reasoning benchmarks show that OPO consistently improves Qwen3-VL-2B and Qwen3-VL-8B, and OPO-8B achieves competitive performance against much larger models and tool-augmented baselines. These results highlight observation policy optimization as an important direction for improving active visual reasoning.
blocks.zh:
在这部作品中,我们研究了工具强化思维与图像的关键挑战:模型不仅必须学习如何理性,还必须学习推理时的视角. 我们显示,在高分辨率细纹视觉任务中的许多失败来自于观测阶段,而不是下游语言推理,而决定当地作物的观察-动作符号表现出的不确定性大大高于普通语言符号. 这些调查结果表明,获取视觉证据是一个关键的决策进程,应当直接加以优化,而不是作为轨道层面生成的普通部分处理。
基于这些观察,我们提议观测政策优化(OPO),通过不确定性引导观测分支和证据本地化优势归属,改善视觉证据的获取. OPO在高不确定性和低冗余观测活动中进行局部分支,使模型能够从共享推理前缀中探索替代作物. 然后,它只向生产相应作物的观察-行动标志物分配证据充足性反馈,从而减少最终答案奖励与当地证据质量之间的信用不匹配。
跨高分辨率视觉推理基准的实验显示,OPO持续改进了Qune3-VL-2B和Qune3-VL-8B,而OPO-8B则相对于更大的模型和工具增强的基线实现竞争性能. 这些成果突出了观察政策优化是改进主动视觉推理的重要方向.

blocks.en: Appendix B Benchmark Details
blocks.zh: 附录B 基准细节

blocks.en:
We evaluate OPO on three high-resolution perception benchmarks:
V* [ 12 ] , HR-Bench 4K, and HR-Bench 8K [ 13 ] .
Following the high-resolution evaluation setting used in DeepEyes [ 7 ] , these benchmarks focus on the ability of models to acquire and interpret fine-grained visual evidence from high-resolution images. Many examples cannot be answered reliably from a global image view or a heavily downsampled image alone; instead, they require models to locate local evidence such as small objects, subtle attributes, local text, or spatial relations.
blocks.zh:
我们根据三个高清感知基准评价业务干事:
V* [12],HR-Bench 4K,以及HR-Bench 8K [13].
在DeepEyes [7] 中使用的高分辨率评价设定之后,这些基准侧重于模型从高分辨率图像中获取和诠释细纹视觉证据的能力. 许多例子无法从全局图像观点或仅从严重下取样的图像中可靠地回答;相反,它们需要模型来定位本地证据,如小物体,微妙属性,本地文本,或空间关系.

blocks.en: V* [ 12 ] focuses on guided visual search over natural images and evaluates whether a model can locate and use critical visual details in high-resolution images. The V* split used in our evaluation contains 191 examples in total, including 115 examples from direct_attributes and 76 examples from relative_position . For V*, we report the benchmark-defined attribute, spatial, and overall accuracies.
blocks.zh: V* [12] 专注于引导视觉搜索相对于自然图像,并评价一个模型是否能够在高分辨率图像中定位和使用关键的视觉细节. 我们评价中使用的V*分法共包含191个实例,包括115个直接属性实例和76个相对位置实例。 对于V*,我们报告基准界定的属性、空间和总体强度。

blocks.en: HR-Bench [ 13 ] contains two high-resolution evaluation versions, HR-Bench 4K and HR-Bench 8K, which measure whether models can resolve local visual evidence under increasingly demanding image resolutions. Each version contains 200 original questions, including 100 Fine-grained Single-instance Perception (FSP) questions and 100 Fine-grained Cross-instance Perception (FCP) questions. FSP evaluates fine-grained perception over a single instance, such as attribute recognition, OCR, and visual prompting, while FCP evaluates fine-grained perception across multiple instances, such as map analysis, chart analysis, and spatial relationship assessment.
blocks.zh: HR-Bench [13] 包含了两个高分辨率的评价版本,HR-Bench 4K和HR-Bench 8K,它们衡量模型是否能够在要求越来越大的图像分辨率下解决局部视觉证据. 每个版本包含200个原始问题,包括100个精细的单倍感(FSP)问题和100个精细的交叉感(FCP)问题. FSP评价一个单一情况下的精致感知,如属性识别,OCR,和视觉提示;而FCP评价多处的精致感知,如地图分析,图表分析,和空间关系评估.

blocks.en: In our evaluation, each original HR-Bench question is expanded into four option-rotation instances. As a result, hr_bench_4k contains 800 evaluation rows and hr_bench_8k contains 800 evaluation rows, yielding 1,600 rows in total. When reporting results, we aggregate performance according to the original benchmark definitions and report FSP, FCP, and overall accuracy following the official scoring protocol.
blocks.zh: 在我们的评价中,每一个最初的HR-Bench问题被扩展为四个可选轮换的情况。 因此,hr_bench_4k包含800个评价行,hr_bench_8k包含800个评价行,共产生1600个评价行. 在报告结果时,我们根据原始基准定义汇总业绩,并报告FSP,FCP,以及官方评分协议之后的总体准确性.

blocks.en: These benchmarks are particularly aligned with our setting because successful prediction often requires an explicit observation action: the model must first decide which local region should be inspected and then answer based on the acquired local evidence. Therefore, for both OPO and our reproduced Qwen3-VL tool-use baselines, we keep the image zoom-in tool enabled during inference. The model is allowed to perform multi-turn tool-augmented reasoning, and we evaluate only the final answer after the trajectory terminates.
blocks.zh: 这些基准特别符合我们的设定,因为成功的预测往往需要明确的观察行动:模型必须首先决定应当检查哪个地区,然后根据获得的当地证据作出答复。 因此,对于OPO和我们复制的Qwen3-VL工具使用基线,我们在推论期间都允许图像缩放工具. 该模型被允许进行多回合工具强化推理,我们仅在轨迹终止后评价最终答案.

blocks.en: Appendix C Evaluation Protocol
blocks.zh: 附录C 评价议定书

blocks.en: We evaluate saved checkpoints with deterministic multi-turn generation. For each benchmark example, we use the same system instructions, response format, and tool schema as in training, and generate one assistant turn at a time using greedy decoding. Each sample allows up to 10 tool-use turns. When the generated response contains a valid <tool_call>...</tool_call> block, the evaluator parses the JSON arguments, converts the bounding box to image coordinates, crops the selected image from the visible image pool, appends the crop as a tool message, and continues generation. The trajectory terminates when an <answer>...</answer> block is produced, an invalid tool call is encountered, or the maximum number of turns is reached.
blocks.zh: 我们以决定性的多回合制来评估已挽救的检查站。 对于每个基准例子,我们使用与训练相同的系统指令,响应格式和工具计划,并使用贪婪的解码时生成一个助手转弯. 每个样本最多可有10个工具使用回合。 当生成的响应包含一个有效的<tool_call>...</tool_call>块时,评估者将 JSON 参数解析,将绑定框转换为图像坐标,从可见图像池中裁剪选定的图像,将裁剪作为工具消息附加,并持续生成. 当生成一个 < answer > ... < / answer > 块、 遇到无效的工具调用或达到最大转弯次数时, 轨迹终止 。

blocks.en: For V*, we evaluate the direct attributes and relative position splits. Each example is treated as a multiple-choice visual question, with the first option as the benchmark-provided correct answer. The final answer is extracted from the answer tags. We apply an LLM judge to compare the model answer with the standard answer using few-shot consistency examples and return a binary judgement. We report accuracy for each split and compute the V* overall score as the mean over all evaluated examples.
blocks.zh: 对于V*,我们评价直接属性和相对位置分裂. 每个例子都被视为一个多选择的视觉问题,第一个选项是基准提供的正确答案. 最后的答案是从答案标记中提取的. 我们应用一个LLM法官来比较模型解答与标准解答,使用几发一致性示例,并返回二进制判断. 我们报告每次拆分的准确性,并计算V*总分,作为所有被评价的例子的平均值。

blocks.en: For HR-Bench, we evaluate the HR-Bench 4K and HR-Bench 8K splits. Images are decoded from the benchmark TSV files and resized according to the Qwen-VL visual grid before inference. The same multi-turn tool loop and answer extraction procedure are used. The judging script reports accuracy separately for the benchmark’s Fine-grained Single-instance Perception (FSP) and Fine-grained Cross-instance Perception (FCP) categories and computes each split’s overall score as the unweighted average of these two category accuracies. These scores correspond to the HR-Bench columns reported in Table 1 .
blocks.zh: 对于HR-Bench,我们评价HR-Bench 4K和HR-Bench 8K的拆分. 图像由基准TSV文件解码,在推论前根据Quen-VL视觉网格调整大小. 使用相同的多回合工具循环和解答提取程序. 判断的脚本分别报告基准的精细单倍感(FSP)和精细单倍感(FCP)类别的精细单倍感(FCP)的准确性,并计算每个分数的总分,作为这两类精细的未加权平均值. 这些分数与表1报告的HR-Bench栏相符。

blocks.en: Appendix D Training Data Details
blocks.zh: 附录D 培训 数据细节

blocks.en: For fair comparison with DeepEyes, we use the same tool-oriented training data recipe rather than constructing a new training corpus. As described in DeepEyes [ 7 ] , the training mixture contains about 47K samples from three complementary sources: Visual Search, ArxivQA, and ThinkLite-VL. Visual Search contributes about 22K samples, roughly 47% of the mixture, and emphasizes natural-image grounding and fine-grained perception. ArxivQA contributes about 14K samples, roughly 30%, covering scientific plots, diagrams, and chart-style visual inputs. ThinkLite-VL contributes about 11K samples, roughly 23%, and provides multimodal reasoning examples involving arithmetic, commonsense inference, and problem solving.
blocks.zh: 为了与DeepEyes进行公平比较,我们使用同样的面向工具的培训数据配方,而不是构建新的培训教材。 如DeepEyes[7]所述,培训混合物包含来自三个补充来源的约47K样本:视觉搜索、ArxivQA和ThinkLite-VL。 视觉搜索贡献了大约22K个样本,约占混合物的47%,强调自然成像地面和精致的感知. 尔十四 质量评估提供了大约14K个样本,约占30%,涵盖科学地块、图表和图表式视觉输入。 ThinkLite-VL提供了大约11K个样本,大约占23%,并提供了涉及算术,常识推论和解决问题的多式联运推理实例.

blocks.en: The DeepEyes data curation process follows a tool-use-oriented filtering pipeline. First, it removes questions that are either too easy or too difficult by estimating model accuracy from multiple responses. Second, it converts questions into an open-ended format and filters unreliable conversions. Third, it removes unverifiable samples, including examples with incorrect answers or unreadable questions. Finally, it prioritizes samples where tool use can improve visual evidence acquisition, especially cases where the model fails from the original image but can answer correctly when given the relevant cropped region. Chart data and reasoning data are retained according to their own preprocessing assumptions because they already provide complementary structured-visual and reasoning supervision.
blocks.zh: DeepEyes数据校验程序遵循一个面向工具的过滤管道。 首先,它通过从多个答复中估计模型的准确性来消除那些太容易或太难的问题。 第二,它把问题转换成不开放的格式,过滤不可靠的转换. 第三,它去除无法验证的样本,包括答案不正确或无法读取的问题的例子. 最后,它优先处理使用工具可以改进视觉证据获取的样本,特别是模型从原始图像中失败,但考虑到相关的裁剪区域,可以正确回答的情况. 图表数据和推理数据根据自己的预处理假设保留,因为它们已经提供了互补的结构-视觉和推理监督.

blocks.en: The image zoom-in tool crops a region from the selected image and returns the cropped image as the next tool observation. The tool maintains a visible image pool consisting of the original input image followed by all tool-returned crops from previous turns. Thus, img_idx=0 refers to the original image, while later indices can refer to earlier crops. For Qwen3-VL models, bounding boxes are interpreted in the normalized [ 0 , 1000 ] [0,1000] coordinate system and converted to image-space pixels before cropping.

blocks.en: Appendix F Reward and Evidence Judge
blocks.zh: 附录F 奖励和证据法官

blocks.en: The reward function has two parts: a trajectory-level final-answer reward and an event-local evidence reward. The final-answer reward first extracts the model’s answer from <answer>...</answer> after the thinking segment. A judge then compares the extracted answer with the ground-truth answer given the original question and returns a binary correctness label. We denote this answer reward by r acc ∈ { 0 , 1 } r_{\mathrm{acc}}\in\{0,1\} . The implementation also includes a tool-use reward r tool r_{\mathrm{tool}} , which is one only when the trajectory uses the zoom-in tool and the final answer is correct, and a format reward r fmt r_{\mathrm{fmt}} , which is − 1 -1 when the response violates the required thinking/answer format and 0 0 otherwise. The global trajectory reward is R global = 0.8 ​ r acc + 1.2 ​ r tool + 0.2 ​ r fmt . R^{\mathrm{global}}=0.8r_{\mathrm{acc}}+1.2r_{\mathrm{tool}}+0.2r_{\mathrm{fmt}}. (14) This global reward is used for the ordinary trajectory-level GRPO signal.

For OPO’s local observation-action supervision, we additionally use an evidence judge. For each branch event, the training pipeline keeps the crops associated with that event and sends each crop, together with the question and ground-truth answer, to a frozen visual judge. The judge must return exactly one of three labels: insufficient , partial , or sufficient . These labels are mapped to local evidence rewards − 1 -1 , 0 0 , and 1 1 , respectively.

blocks.en: Appendix G Qualitative Results
blocks.zh: 附录G 定性 结果

blocks.en: Figure 5 and Figure 6 show qualitative comparisons between direct Qwen3-VL-8B inference and OPO-8B. In the direct-attribute example (Figure 5 ), direct Qwen3-VL-8B inference is distracted by salient but irrelevant yellow regions, such as the pedestrian-crossing sign, and mistakenly treats them as evidence for the color of the cyclist’s box. In contrast, OPO-8B focuses its observation action on the cyclist and the attached box, correctly identifying the box as green from localized evidence. In the spatial-relation example (Figure 6 , top), Qwen3-VL-8B observes both the cone and the baby carriage but fails to reliably resolve their left-right relation; OPO-8B instead crops a local region containing both objects and correctly determines that the carriage is to the right of the cone. In the HR-Bench example (Figure 6 , bottom), Qwen3-VL-8B relies on a coarse building-level observation and mistakes the signboard for an oval shape, whereas OPO-8B accurately localizes the small signboard and zooms into it, allowing it to recognize its rectangular shape from the clear edges and background. These cases show that OPO’s gains do not merely come from invoking the zoom-in tool, but from more reliably selecting question-relevant and evidence-sufficient observation regions, thereby grounding the final answer in localized visual evidence.
blocks.zh: 图5和图6显示了直接Quen3-VL-8B推论和OPO-8B之间的定性比较. 在直接属性例子(图5)中,直接的Qwen3-VL-8B推论被突出但无关紧要的黄色区域,如行人过道标志所分心,并错误地把它们当作自行车手盒颜色的证据. 相比之下,OPO-8B将其观测动作的焦点放在了循环器和所附的盒上,从局部证据中正确识别箱为绿色. 在空间关系例子(图6,顶部)中,Qune3-VL-8B同时观察圆锥体和婴儿车厢,但未能可靠地解决其左-右关系;OPO-8B相反,收割了包含两个物体的局部区域,并正确确定车厢位于圆锥体右侧. 在HR-Bench的例子(图6,下方)中,Qune3-VL-8B依赖于粗细的建筑层观测,错误地将标志牌用于椭圆形状,而OPO-8B则精确地将小的标志牌定位并缩放进去,使其能从清晰的边缘和背景识别其长方形. 这些案件表明,OPO的收益不仅来自使用放大工具,还来自更可靠地选择与问题相关和证据充足的观察区域,从而将最后答案建立在局部视觉证据上。

blocks.en: Appendix H Implementation Details
blocks.zh: 附录H 执行情况 细节

blocks.en: In the main implementation, the rollout budget is M = 8 M=8 , with B = 2 B=2 base rollouts and P = 6 P=6 remaining trajectories for event-local branching and backfill. The pre-action baseline window is W = 16 W=16 , and event uncertainty is computed only from the bounding-box token span, without using image-index or post-crop tokens. Branches preserve the pre-event prefix and resample the suffix from the prompt-plus-prefix state. If the total number of trajectories remains below M M , ordinary rollouts are used as backfill. For local attribution, the local token spans cover image-index, region-label, and bounding-box tokens, and the local advantage is computed only from the event-local evidence reward.
blocks.zh: 在主要实施中,推出预算为M=8 M=8,其中B=2 B=2基础推出,P=6 P=6剩余轨迹用于事件-局部分支和回填. 动作前基线窗口为W=16 W=16,事件不确定性只从边框符号跨度计算,不使用图像索引或作物后符号. 分支保留了事件前缀,并将后缀从即时加前缀状态中重现出来. 如果轨迹总数仍然低于M M ,则使用普通的展开作为回填. 就本地归属而言,本地标志跨度包括图像索引、区域标签和定界框标志,本地优势仅从事件-本地证据奖励计算。

blocks.en: Appendix I Localization Failures in Stronger Models
blocks.zh: 附录一 较强模型的本地化失败

blocks.en: To examine whether the observation bottleneck persists in stronger models, we evaluate Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct, Qwen3.7-Max, and Kimi K3 on all 191 examples in V*. We analyze their inference trajectories without applying OPO training. We manually inspect each unsuccessful trajectory, including incorrect responses and cases without a valid final answer. A trajectory is classified as a localization failure when failure to acquire the visual evidence needed to answer the question is the primary cause of the unsuccessful response.
blocks.zh: 为了检查观测瓶颈是否在更强的模型中持续存在,我们对V*中的所有191个例子评价Qune3-VL-32B-Instruct,Qune3.7-Max和Kimi K3. 我们分析他们的推论轨迹 不应用OPO训练。 我们手动检查每一个不成功的轨迹,包括不正确的反应和没有有效最后答复的案件。 当未能获得回答问题所需的视觉证据是答复失败的主要原因时,轨迹被归类为本地化故障.

blocks.en: Table 4: Localization failures in stronger models on V*. Percentages in the last column are computed over unsuccessful trajectories.
blocks.zh: 表4:V*上较强模型的本地化失败. 最后一栏中的百分比是按不成功的轨迹计算的。

blocks.en: As shown in Table 4 , the three models achieve an aggregate accuracy of 91.3%, yet localization failures account for 41 of their 50 unsuccessful trajectories (82.0%). This pattern appears in all three models: localization failures account for 17/22 unsuccessful trajectories for Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct, 15/19 for Kimi K3, and 9/9 for Qwen3.7-Max. Under the evaluated observation interface, acquiring fine-grained visual evidence thus remains a major source of failure even for stronger models. These findings motivate extending observation-policy optimization to larger backbones and additional model families, with controlled OPO training as a direction for future work.
blocks.zh: 如表4所示,三种模型的总精度为91.3%,而本地化失败则占其50种不成功的轨迹中的41种(82.0%)。 这种模式在所有三种模型中都出现:本地化故障占Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct的17/22不成功的轨迹,Kimi K3的15/19和Quen3.7-Max的9/9. 因此,在经过评价的观测界面下,获取精细的视觉证据,即使是更强大的模型,仍然是失败的主要原因。 这些调查结果促使观察政策优化扩大到更大的骨干和更多的模范家庭,以受控的OPO培训作为未来工作的方向.

blocks.en: Appendix J Limitations and Future Work
blocks.zh: 附录J 限制和今后的工作

blocks.en: Our work focuses on optimizing observation actions under an image zoom-in tool. This setting directly targets a key bottleneck in high-resolution fine-grained perception, where the model must decide where to look in order to acquire useful local evidence. However, tool-augmented visual reasoning in more general scenarios may involve a broader set of tools, such as OCR, detection, segmentation, search, code execution, or more complex image manipulation tools. Therefore, our current experiments do not fully characterize how OPO generalizes to a more diverse tool ecosystem.
blocks.zh: 我们的工作重点是在图像放大工具下优化观察行动。 这种设定直接针对高分辨率精细感知中的关键瓶颈,模型必须决定在哪里寻找才能获得有用的当地证据. 然而,在更一般的情景中,工具强化的视觉推理可能涉及更广泛的一组工具,如OCR,检测,分割,搜索,代码执行,或更复杂的图像操纵工具. 因此,我们目前的实验并未充分说明OPO如何将一般化为更加多样化的工具生态系统。

blocks.en: Second, due to computational and time constraints, we train and evaluate OPO mainly on Qwen3-VL-2B and Qwen3-VL-8B, rather than further applying it to newer or stronger native multimodal backbones such as Qwen3.5. As a result, although our experiments show that OPO remains effective when scaling from 2B to 8B models, its behavior on larger and more capable backbone models remains to be further validated.
blocks.zh: 第二,由于计算和时间的限制,我们主要在Qun3-VL-2B和Qun3-VL-8B上训练和评价OPO,而不是进一步将其应用于较新或较强的本土多式联运骨干,如Qun3.5. 因此,虽然我们的实验表明OPO在从2B模型缩放到8B模型时依然有效,但其在更大和更有能力的主干模型上的行为仍有待进一步验证.

blocks.en: Future work can extend OPO in two main directions. First, OPO can be generalized to broader visual and multimodal tools, enabling models to learn not only where to look, but also when to invoke different tools and how to combine them for evidence acquisition. Second, applying OPO to stronger native multimodal models would further test its scalability and clarify whether observation-action optimization can complement stronger visual encoders, longer-context reasoning, and more general tool-use capabilities.
blocks.zh: 今后的工作可以在两个主要方向上扩展OPO. 首先,OPO可以被泛指到更广泛的视觉和多式联运工具,使模型不仅能够学习在哪里寻找,而且能够学习何时使用不同的工具以及如何将它们结合起来获取证据。 第二,将OPO应用于更强大的本土多式联运模式将进一步测试其可扩展性,并澄清观察-动作优化能否补充更强的视觉编码器、较长的文字推理和更一般的工具使用能力。

blocks.en: Appendix K Societal Impacts
blocks.zh: 附录K 社会 影响

blocks.en: OPO aims to improve the ability of vision-language models to acquire fine-grained visual evidence from high-resolution images. This can have positive impacts in applications that require careful inspection of visual details, such as document understanding, chart analysis, scientific image interpretation, accessibility tools, and assistance with complex visual question answering. By making observation actions more reliable, the method may also reduce failures where a model answers from insufficient or irrelevant visual evidence.
blocks.zh: OPO旨在提高视觉语言模型从高分辨率图像中获取精致视觉证据的能力. 这对需要仔细检查视觉细节的应用具有积极影响,例如文件理解、图表分析、科学图像判读、无障碍工具以及协助回答复杂的视觉问题。 通过使观测动作更加可靠,当模型从不充分或不相关的视觉证据中解答时,这种方法还可能减少故障.

blocks.en: At the same time, stronger tool-augmented visual reasoning systems may introduce risks if deployed without appropriate oversight. More reliable zooming and local evidence acquisition could be misused for privacy-invasive visual analysis, automated surveillance, or high-stakes decision making where model errors are difficult for users to detect. The method may also increase user trust in generated answers even when the acquired evidence is incomplete or the evidence judge is miscalibrated.
blocks.zh: 同时,如果在没有适当监督的情况下部署更强大的工具增强的视觉推理系统,可能会带来风险。 更可靠的缩放和本地证据获取可能会被滥用于隐私入侵视觉分析,自动监控,或者在模式错误难以被用户发现的情况下,高调决策. 该方法还可能提高用户对生成的答案的信任度,即使获得的证据不完整或证据裁判员判断错误.

blocks.en: NeurIPS Paper Checklist
blocks.zh: 神经病 纸张核对表

blocks.en: 1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The abstract and introduction make claims that accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] Justification: This paper discusses the limitations of the work in the Appendix. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [N/A] Justification: There is no theoretical results. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: This work provides all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper in the Implementation Details. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The code is publicly available at https://github.com/Yann0122/Observation-Policy-Optimization . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The experimental setups, including data splits, training, and testing details, are provided in the Method and Experiments sections. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [No] Justification: We follow the default evaluations in the vision-language models field, which do not require error bars. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We provide them in the implementation details of the main paper and the Appendix. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] Justification: This work conforms to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The broader impacts are provided in the Appendix. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The proposed method uses pre-trained models. This proposed method is safe under the safeguards of adopted pre-trained models. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We cited the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators. 13. New assets Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The code and accompanying documentation have been publicly released at https://github.com/Yann0122/Observation-Policy-Optimization . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file. 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector. 15. Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained? Answer: [N/A] Justification: There is no research with human subjects in this work. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review. 16. Declaration of LLM usage Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required. Answer: [Yes] Justification: We describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
blocks.zh: 一、导 言 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 抽象和导言提出了准确反映文件的贡献和范围的要求。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指摘要和导言不包括文件中的主张。 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 审议人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的[不]或[不]的答复。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是]理由: 本文件讨论了附录中工作的局限性。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另辟一个“限制”部分。 文件应说明任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设遭到违反(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)的结果如何有力。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何遭到违反,其影响如何。 作者应思考所提出主张的范围,例如,如果这一办法只在几个数据集或几个运行中测试。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,这些假设应当加以阐述。 作者应反思影响该办法执行的因素。 例如,一个面部识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像在低光照下拍摄时可能表现不佳. 或语音对文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论提议的算法的计算效率以及它们如何用数据集大小来进行比例。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的办法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会以完全诚实的限度作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中不承认的限制。 作者应运用最佳判断,承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社会完整性的规范方面发挥着重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚在限制方面的诚实。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 答复:[不详]理由: 没有理论结果。 准则: • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括理论结果. • 支助 所有论文中的定理,公式和证明,都应该编号,相互参照. • 支助 所有假设都应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在主要论文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证据草图以提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据都应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:[是]理由: 这项工作提供了在《执行细节》中转载该文件的主要实验结果所需的所有资料。 • 答案[N/A]是指论文不包括实验。 如果论文包括实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或可核查而采取的步骤。 • 根据贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一个具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人能够用相同的数据集复制这个模型,或者提供对模型的访问. 总论中. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一点的好办法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. • 支助 虽然NeurIPS不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交材料提供一些合理的可复制途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当明确说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范结构,文件应清楚、全面地描述这种结构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者描述它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 对于封闭源代码模型,可能以某种方式限制对模型的获取(如注册用户),但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码 文件是否提供了开放的数据和代码,并有足够的指示,如补充材料所述,忠实地复制主要实验结果? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 该守则可在https://github.com/Yann0122/Observation-Policy-Optiimization上公开查阅。 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括需要代码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmission Policy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而拒绝文件,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). • 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何获取原始数据、预先处理的数据、中间数据以及生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本,复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验是可复制的,它们应该说明哪些实验从脚本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为保持匿名,提交人应公布匿名版本(如果适用)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的信息(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(如数据分割、超参数、如何选择、优化者的类型)? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 方法和实验部分提供了实验设置,包括数据分割、培训和测试细节。 • 答案[N/A]是指论文不包括实验。 实验环境应在文件核心中详细介绍,以便了解结果,使之合理。 详细情况可通过附录中的代码或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告错误是否含有适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:理由: 我们跟踪视觉语言模型领域的默认评价,这些评价不需要错误栏。 • 答案[N/A]是指论文不包括实验。 如果结果附有错误栏、信任间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕捉的可变因素(例如,列车/测试拆分、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算错误栏的方法应加以解释(封闭格式公式、调用库函数、靴子陷阱等) —— 应给出假设(例如,通常分布错误)。 应明确误差栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准误差. ^ 报告1-西格玛错误栏是正常的,但应该说明这一点。 如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,提交人最好报告2-西格玛错误栏,而不是说他们有96%的CI。 • 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称误差栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负误差率). • 支助 如果在表格或图中报告错误栏,作者应在文字中解释它们是如何计算的,并在文字中参考相应的数字或表格。 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们在主要文件和附录的执行细节中提供了这些建议。 • 答案[N/A]是指论文不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额,并估计计算总额。 论文应披露完整的研究项目是否比论文中报告的实验需要更多的计算(例如初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写进论文中). 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复:[是]理由: 这项工作符合《新IPS道德守则》。 • 答案[N/A]意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应该解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例受到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题:本文件是否讨论所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和消极社会影响? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 附录提供了更广泛的影响。 · 答案[N/A]是指所进行的工作没有社会影响。 如果作者回答[N/A]或[否],他们应当解释他们的工作为何没有社会影响,或为何文件没有涉及社会影响。 • 支助 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或意外使用(例如:造谣、制造假面貌、监视)、公平考虑(例如:采用可能作出对特定群体造成不公平影响的决定的技术)、隐私考虑和安全考虑。 会议期望许多论文将是基础研究,而不是与特定应用挂钩,更不用说部署. 然而,如果有任何否定性申请的直接途径,提交人应当指出。 例如,可以合理地指出,可以利用基因模型质量的提高来产生用于造谣的Deepfakes. 另一方面,不需要指出优化神经网络的通用算法可以让人们训练出更快生成Deepfake的模型. ^ . 作者应考虑在技术作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及(有意或无意)滥用技术造成的伤害。 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行封闭释放,在攻击之外提供防御,监测误用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中吸取教训的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。 11. 保障问题: 文件是否描述了为负责任地发布具有高度滥用风险的数据或模型(如预先培训的语言模型、图像生成器或报废数据集)而实施的保障措施? 答复:[不详]理由: 提议的方法采用预先训练的模型。 这一拟议方法在已采用的预先培训的模型的保障下是安全的。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件没有构成这种风险。 • 释放的具有高度滥用或双重用途风险的模型,应附带必要的保障措施,允许控制使用该模型,例如要求用户遵守使用准则或限制进入模型或实施安全过滤器。 • 支助 从互联网上拆掉的数据集可能构成安全风险。 作者应说明如何避免释放不安全的图像。 我们认识到,提供有效的保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点,并作出最大的诚意努力。 12. 现有资产的许可证问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有人,是否适当贷记,许可证和使用条款是否明确提及和适当遵守? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们引用了产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应包含每项资产。 • 支助 对于从某一特定来源(如网站)提取的数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于流行的数据集来说,使用code.com/dataset的文档拥有一些数据集的许可证。 它们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 • 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。 13. 新资产问题:文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,是否与资产一起提供文件? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 在https://github.com/Yann0122/Observation-Policy-Optimization 上,已公开发布代码和所附文件。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不释放新资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板,将数据集/代码/模型的细节作为提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 该文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。 14. 人口集中和人类课题研究 关于众包实验和与人类主体的研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示全文和(如果适用的话)截图,以及(如果有)补偿的细节? 答复:[不详]理由: 论文不涉及众包,也不涉及人类主体的研究. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 将这一资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主题,那么应在主要文件中尽可能详细。 • 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、整理或其他工作的工人应至少领取数据收集国的最低工资。 15. 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或相当于与人有关的研究 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向主体披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得同等的批准/审查)? 答复:[不详]理由: 这项工作没有涉及人类学科的研究。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 视进行研究的国家而定,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于批准)。 - 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在报纸上明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 • 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性的信息(如果适用的话),例如进行审查的机构。 16. 关于LLM使用的声明问题: 论文是否描述了LLMs的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于书写、编辑或格式化目的,且不影响研究的核心方法、科学严谨性或原创性,则不需要宣布。 答复:[是]理由: 我们描述LLMS的使用,如果它是这一研究的核心方法的重要、原始或非标准的组成部分。 · 答案[N/A]是指本研究的核心方法开发并不涉及作为任何重要、原始或非标准组成部分的法学硕士。 请参看NeurIPS手册中我们的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。

blocks.zh: 索偿

blocks.en: Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope?
blocks.zh: 问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: The abstract and introduction make claims that accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 抽象和导言提出了准确反映文件的贡献和范围的要求。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指摘要和导言不包括文件中的主张。 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 审议人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的[不]或[不]的答复。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。

blocks.en: The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper.
blocks.zh: 答案[N/A]指抽象和导言不包括论文中的说法.

blocks.en: The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers.

blocks.en: The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings.
blocks.zh: 所提出的索赔应当与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果能够归纳到其他环境。

blocks.zh: 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.

However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out.
